title: Prompt-cache forensics from 30 real sessions: 68% of cache writes come from 36 events (TTL expiry, microcompact, resume) — with paper-backed mitigations
excerpt:
*Measured 13/09/2026 by one user: Windows 11, Claude desktop app, Claude Code 2.1.266, Opus 5 / Fable 5.1, 1M context enabled. Version numbers as reported by the app.*

## TL;DR

- Across 30 sessions (3,203 API calls), **cache reads are 64% of API-equivalent cost**, cache writes 28%, output 9%. Average context per call is **320k tokens** (median 239k, p90 707k). The system-prompt prefix is ~83k of that (49k shared across projects + ~34k project-specific); **the rest is conversation history**.
- **68% of all cache-write tokens (14.8M of 21.7M) come from 36 events**, not from steady-state growth. Three causes, all client-observable:
  1. **1h TTL expiry** — 19 events, 9.4M tokens. Expected, but each one re-writes 300–860k of history.
  2. **Mid-history pruning (microcompact)** — 4 events in one session, 3.0M tokens. Each time ~83k of old tool results were cleared, `cache_read` fell to the shared prefix (47,638) and 620–830k were re-written. Once it happened **two calls after** a TTL re-write: 1.3M tokens written inside one minute, where a prune aligned to the cold miss would have cost nothing extra.
  3. **Resume / model switch** — ~6 events, ~1.9M tokens. On resume `cache_read` equals the *shared* prefix only (49,043), so the project part of the system prompt is not byte-stable across sessions and the whole history is re-written behind it.
- The suggestions below are small and mostly scheduling: prune when the cache is already cold, prune in bigger batches, keep the project prefix byte-stable on resume, and consider a bounded-history default. Each has a paper behind it (section 4).
- A measurement pitfall worth documenting: **the session `.jsonl` writes one `assistant` line per content block (thinking / text / tool_use), each carrying the same `usage`.** Summing usage per line overstates everything ~1.7×. Dedup by `(message.id, requestId)`.

## 1. Method

- Source: `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl`, the 30 most recently modified sessions (25 with ≥5 calls). Only `type == "assistant"` entries with `message.usage`.
- Dedup by `(message.id, requestId)` → 5,568 lines become 3,203 calls.
- "Cache break" = a call whose `cache_creation_input_tokens` exceeds 20% of the previous call's total context and 20k tokens. Classified by wall-clock gap to the previous call (>60 min → TTL), by whether the context shrank, and by what happened between the two calls (

title: [Feature Request] Unified user state across Cowork and Claude chat — shared memory, files, skills, connectors
excerpt:
## Problem

Claude Cowork (Desktop research preview) and Claude chat (web + iOS + Android) operate as siloed surfaces despite serving the same authenticated user:

- Cowork can read/write a scoped folder on my Mac, run skills, use plugins, and execute multi-step file-centric work — but only at my desk, with no mobile equivalent.
- Chat (especially the iOS app) is where I actually spend time when I'm away from my desk. It has its own memory, its own connectors, its own thread history.

When I shift surfaces during a workflow, context resets. Memory doesn't follow. Files I worked on in Cowork aren't visible in chat on the go. Connector state and authentications don't carry. Skills configured for one don't appear in the other (related: #20697).

## Use case

Typical day: morning at desk → Cowork on a project folder → commute → continue thinking in iOS chat → evening back at desk → Cowork to execute. Today this requires manual context-passing. I use Claude Code Dispatch from iOS to route specific tasks to a Claude Code session on my Mac, which works well, but it doesn't solve the underlying memory and file split — it just routes a single task across.

I've worked around this by making Obsidian Sync my canonical file backend (Claude Code reads it directly on Mac, Obsidian Sync handles mobile access), but that only partially closes the gap and doesn't address memory or connector state.

## Suggested approach

Treat Cowork and chat as two surfaces over a single unified user state:

1. **Shared memory** — claude.ai memory, Cowork auto-memory, and Claude Code CLAUDE.md should converge into one coherent layer the user can read/write from any surface.
2. **Shared file workspace** — when Cowork has a folder scoped, that folder (or selected artifacts) should be reachable from chat as a viewable/searchable resource. From iOS I should be able to ask "what's the latest on the X analysis I was working on in Cowork?" and get an answer grounded in Cowork's actual files.
3. **Shared skills and connectors** — already requested for skills in #20697; extend to connectors and authentication state.
4. **Surface handoff affordances** — explicit "continue this in Cowork" / "continue this in chat" actions, analogous to Claude Code's `/desktop` and `--teleport` for the coding case.

- #2511 — Claude Code ↔ Claude Projects

title: Expose rate-limit reset times, balance, plan as status_line tokens
excerpt:
## Summary

The CLI status_line exposes `five-hour-limit` and `weekly-limit` as percentages only. The underlying rate-limit data is richer — `account/rateLimits/read` returns `resetsAt`, `windowDurationMins`, `credits.balance`, `planType` — but those fields aren't reachable via status_line tokens.

## Missing tokens (as of 0.133.0)

1. `five-hour-limit-reset` — formatted local time of `primary.resetsAt`
2. `weekly-limit-reset` — formatted local time of `secondary.resetsAt`
3. `credits-balance` — `credits.balance` (e.g. `$766.76`) when `credits.hasCredits && !credits.unlimited`
4. `plan-type` — `planType` (e.g. `prolite`)
5. (optional) `rate-limit-window-primary` / `-secondary` — `windowDurationMins` formatted

## Use case

Mirrors Claude Code's statusline which shows percentage + reset time. Without reset times the bare percentage is hard to act on — "5h 80%" doesn't tell you whether you have 10 minutes or 3 hours of breathing room. With it:

```
... · 5h 80% @11:36pm · weekly 83% @5/27 5:40am · ...
```

## Workaround

Spawn `codex app-server` from outside, JSON-RPC handshake, call `account/rateLimits/read`, parse, render. Works but adds ~3-5s subprocess startup per query and requires users to build their own caching layer. The data is already there inside the running CLI; surfacing it as a token is a small change.

## Verified data shape (0.133.0)

`account/rateLimits/read` returns:

```json
{
  "rateLimits": {
    "limitId": "codex",
    "primary": { "usedPercent": 25, "windowDurationMins": 300, "resetsAt": 1779459394 },
    "secondary": { "usedPercent": 18, "windowDurationMins": 10080, "resetsAt": 1779826837 },
    "credits": { "hasCredits": true, "unlimited": false, "balance": "766.76..." },
    "planType": "prolite",
    "rateLimitReachedType": null
  },
  "rateLimitsByLimitId": { ... }
}
```

## Acceptance

Adding these to the existing config:

```toml
status_line = ["model-with-reasoning", "codex-version", "context-remaining",
               "five-hour-limit", "five-hour-limit-reset",
               "weekly-limit", "weekly-limit-reset",
               "credits-balance", "project", "git-branch"]
```

Produces:

```
gpt-5.5 high · 0.133.0 · Context 28% left · 5h 25% @11:36pm · weekly 18% @5/27 5:40am · $766.76 · self-service-workbench · main
```

Thanks for the great CLI.

Visible website permissions and stored global allow rules disagree with the chat-scoped denial. The user cannot complete authorized desktop/mobile QA of their website.

Diagnosis scope
The files confirm conflicting global and session permissions. This suggests precedence or invalidation behavior, but the exact application-level cause has not been established. No permission files were modified, no policy bypass attempted. No credentials, customer data, chat ID, or raw transcripts are included.

Request
Please document a supported session-denial reset or fix invalidation of stale per-chat origin decisions when the user explicitly changes website permissions.

title: [BUG] Headless chrome.exe launched by Claude Code on Windows triggers failed logons and locks IdP-managed accounts
excerpt:
## Summary

On Windows 11 devices managed by an identity provider (JumpCloud), each time Claude Code launches `chrome.exe` (or `msedge.exe`) in headless mode from the shell to convert local HTML into PDF/PNG, Windows records a burst of failed logon attempts attributed to the browser process. The identity provider counts them as wrong-password attempts and locks the user's account. No password is being typed; the only trigger is the headless browser launch.

## Environment

- Claude Code desktop app on Windows 11 Pro, devices bound to JumpCloud
- Users who ask Claude Code for PDFs/images rendered from HTML get locked out; users with the same software who never ask for that never do
- Does not reproduce on macOS with the same workflow

## Evidence

On one affected machine, 6 of 7 failed-login bursts over two days match, to the minute, a headless Chrome launch by a Claude Code session (screenshots of a local HTML deck, HTML to PDF, a script rendering images). Attempts inside a burst are 1.5 to 3 s apart and keep going after the account is already locked. JumpCloud's troubleshooting docs note that browser automation tools can trigger a Chromium defect that produces failed logins per session, which matches.

## Expected

Rendering a local HTML file with headless Chrome should not generate Windows credential validation attempts.

## Workaround applied

Global CLAUDE.md rule for Windows users: never invoke `chrome.exe`/`msedge.exe` headless to convert HTML; hand the HTML to the user or produce .docx/.pptx instead.

## Asks

1. Does the default HTML to PDF/PNG path on Windows launch headless Chrome with the user's default profile? A temporary `--user-data-dir` plus `--no-first-run --disable-sync` may avoid whatever triggers the credential check.
2. A built-in renderer or a documented safe set of flags for Windows would prevent silent lockouts on SSO-managed devices.

Happy to share Windows Security event 4625 details (LogonType/SubStatus) once collected.

This is the latest Astation-to-Atem handoff for independent remote clients. Please review the joint contract decisions before implementing admission or emitting new signed push fields.

Sources:
- Astation draft PR #58: https://github.com/Agora-Build/Astation/pull/58
- Reviewed handoff snapshot: Astation commit a9e850a0a76e81b131697fe1ce8ee8fb076be108.
- Remote/API design: https://github.com/Agora-Build/Astation/blob/a9e850a0a76e81b131697fe1ce8ee8fb076be108/designs/protocol/remote-agent-api.md
- Signed push/scheduler proposal: https://github.com/Agora-Build/Astation/blob/a9e850a0a76e81b131697fe1ce8ee8fb076be108/designs/protocol/approval-push-proof.md
- Current readable copies (VPN): https://truck.netbird.cloud:58310/protocol/remote-agent-api.md and https://truck.netbird.cloud:58310/protocol/approval-push-proof.md

## Product requirements

1. Mobile/native Astation connects independently to the original Atem host, whether Mac Astation is online or offline. Mac and mobile can view the same original agent sessions concurrently. The Atem host itself must remain running/reachable. Each controller has its own enrolled keys and attachment; no dependency on the Mac's local API or borrowed credentials.
2. Keep r8 operation semantics: one terminal/control lease per agent session; prompt Send atomically acquires an unowned lease, and taking another holder requires confirmed expected-controller takeover. Approval answers and rule revocation are lease-free with control permission and the exact request/rule. Reading or approving on mobile must not disturb the Mac's lease. Reconnect never silently regains control.
3. Use WSS first. A later Agora Signaling adapter may improve end-user connectivity, but must preserve endpoint proof, encryption, ordering, target/lease fencing and durable receipts. Verify runtime/platform and network support before enabling it. Whole-message responses are sufficient; token-by-token streaming is not required.
4. Preserve rich response content. Existing text parts already carry Markdown; retain original source, typed tool/approval parts, IDs and ordering in live/history/API delivery. Mobile will render paragraphs, headings, bold/italic, highlighted links, lists, code blocks with highlighting/copy, and tables. Basic formatting needs no new host message type. Images/audio/PDF/files are separate capabilities and must not be implied by Markdown supp
